summary: Reverse engineering: read a compiled program's logic to find the hidden answer (a check on input, an embedded flag, or a key-derivation). Workflow: identify the format/packing -> static read of the check -> dynamic confirm -> invert the check (by hand, or with angr/z3).
quick_triage: file ./bin ; strings -n 6 ./bin | grep -iE 'flag|ctf|key|pass|correct|wrong'  (sometimes the flag is just there).
Detect packing: `file` says 'UPX'? high entropy? -> unpack first (upx -d).
Pick the right tool by format: native ELF/PE -> Ghidra/IDA/r2; .NET -> dnSpy/ILSpy; Java -> jadx/CFR; Android APK -> jadx/apktool; Python -> pyinstxtractor + decompyle3; wasm -> wasm2wat.
Find the comparison that gates success (strcmp, memcmp, custom loop). The flag is whatever makes it pass.
If input is transformed then compared to a constant, INVERT the transform. If the transform is complex, use angr or z3 to solve for the input.
Confirm dynamically: ltrace/strace, or gdb breakpoint on the compare to read the expected buffer.

tools.name: Ghidra
tools.when: Primary decompiler for native ELF/PE/Mach-O — free, scriptable.
tools.usage: Import -> analyze -> read decompiled function; rename vars; use the Script Manager for bulk work

tools.name: IDA Free
tools.when: Alternative decompiler; great graph view (cloud decompiler in Free).

tools.name: radare2 / rizin + Cutter
tools.when: Scriptable CLI RE and a free GUI (Cutter) with decompiler plugins.
tools.usage: r2 -A ./bin; afl; pdf @ sym.main; Cutter for GUI

tools.name: gdb + pwndbg/gef
tools.when: Dynamic analysis: breakpoint the check, read registers/memory, patch live.

tools.name: ltrace / strace
tools.when: See library/syscalls at runtime — often reveals strcmp(input, FLAG) directly.

tools.name: angr
tools.when: Symbolic execution: auto-find the input that reaches 'Correct' — the rev workhorse for keygen-style checks.

tools.name: z3-solver
tools.when: Model a constraint check (XOR/arith loops) and solve for the flag bytes.
tools.usage: from z3 import *; s=Solver(); s.add(...); s.check(); s.model()

tools.name: dnSpy / ILSpy
tools.when: .NET assemblies — full decompile + live edit/debug (dnSpy on Windows; ILSpy/ilspycmd cross-platform).

install.note: dnSpyEx release; or `dotnet tool install ilspycmd -g`

tools.usage: Open .exe/.dll -> read C#; dnSpy can edit+save to bypass checks

tools.name: jadx
tools.when: Android APK / Java — decompile DEX/JAR to readable Java.

tools.name: apktool
tools.usage: apktool d app.apk ; apktool b app

tools.name: pyinstxtractor + decompyle3/uncompyle6
tools.when: PyInstaller exe or .pyc back to Python source.

tools.name: frida
tools.when: Dynamic instrumentation: hook functions at runtime, dump args/return (mobile + native).

tools.name: binwalk
tools.when: Firmware / embedded blobs: find and extract filesystems and nested binaries.

tools.name: Binary Ninja
tools.when: Strong decompiler/analysis with a clean Python API (free cloud tier); good when Ghidra's output is messy.
tools.usage: open binary -> HLIL/decompiler; scriptable via Python API

tools.name: Androguard
tools.when: Reverse-engineer Android APKs programmatically (DEX analysis, call graphs).

tools.name: Krakatau
tools.when: Java bytecode decompiler + disassembler (alternative to jadx/CFR).
